messages.author: e9cc24d7b29070f1
messages.subject: SAM for nested data.
parts:
Dear all,

I just ran (global) SAM (lavaan 0.6-9) using a nested data and I don’t think any robust.cluster algorithm is used. I put the “cluster” argument as in SEM() function and model fits results are the same as without such argument (only tiny differences in AIC, BIC, and SRMR). SEM function shows two columns: Standard and Robust. SAM only shows one column, and this may be like Standard in SEM, however SAM procedure knows the existence of clusters because the number of them is provided.

My first question: Will a robust.cluster algorithm be implemented in SAM in a near future? In next release?

My second question: I have 128 observations (39 clusters) for 63 free parameters, I hesitate to fit a SEM model (to use the same words as in the draft paper of reference), Robust-SEM model fits are magnificent (no improper solution at all). Could I use Robust-SEM? Without Robust-SAM (the expected solution), model fits worsen (approaching Standard-SEM).

Thank you very much in advance for your collaboration.

Xavier

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: SAM for nested data.
parts: I don’t think any robust.cluster algorithm is used

Correct, none has been developed.  Read the under-review preprint that is linked on the ?sam help page, and you will see in the Discussion that this has only been developed so far for the ideal case of normal, single-level data without missing values.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: SAM for nested data.
parts:
I am afraid 'cluster robust' standard errors are not available in the
SAM framework yet. This is work in progress...

Yves.
